case.question: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?
case.note: Definitions §3 sets the promotion dates, lunch hours, and two sales channels. The prompt defines lift as the change from the same dates a year earlier. Comparing with the previous month instead gives a gross sales increase of $4,442 rather than $5,272.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-01: Compared with the same four weeks last year, how much more did lunch bring in during the Lunch 20 promo?

WITH lunch AS (
  SELECT gross_sales_cents, created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago' AS local_time
  FROM orders
  WHERE state = 'completed'
    AND channel IN ('in_store', 'square_online')
)
SELECT sum(gross_sales_cents) FILTER (WHERE local_time::date BETWEEN '2026-08-03' AND '2026-08-30')
     - sum(gross_sales_cents) FILTER (WHERE local_time::date BETWEEN '2025-08-03' AND '2025-08-30')
FROM lunch
WHERE extract(hour FROM local_time) BETWEEN 11 AND 13

case.question: How many regulars did we lose over the summer?
case.note: Definitions §4 defines regulars as customers with at least three orders from March through May. A regular is counted as lost if they have not ordered since the end of August. Of 599 regulars, 177 meet that condition.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-03: How many regulars did we lose over the summer?

WITH visits AS (
  SELECT customer_id, (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago')::date AS local_day
  FROM orders
  WHERE state = 'completed'
    AND customer_id IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT count(*)
FROM (
  SELECT customer_id
  FROM visits
  GROUP BY customer_id
  HAVING count(*) FILTER (WHERE local_day BETWEEN '2026-03-01' AND '2026-05-31') >= 3
     AND count(*) FILTER (WHERE local_day > '2026-08-31') = 0
) lost_regulars

case.question: Which side dish earns us the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, after Uber's commission and food cost?
case.note: The prompt defines item margin after commission and food cost. Marketplace Terms §2 sets Uber Eats delivery commission at 30%. Pickled Vegetables has the lowest margin at $1.55 per unit, followed by Fried Egg at $1.61.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-04: Which side dish earns us the least per unit on Uber Eats delivery, after Uber's commission and food cost?

SELECT i.name
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN items i ON i.id = oi.item_id
JOIN categories c ON c.id = i.category_id
WHERE o.state = 'completed'
  AND o.channel = 'uber_eats'
  AND o.fulfillment_type = 'delivery'
  AND c.name = 'Sides'
GROUP BY i.name, i.cost_cents
ORDER BY avg(oi.unit_price_cents) * 0.70 - i.cost_cents
LIMIT 1

case.question: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?
case.note: The prompt defines net payout after card fees for in-store orders and after the 25% commission for DoorDash delivery. The averages are $30.11 in store and $27.47 on DoorDash, a $2.64 difference, even with the 25% marketplace price markup.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-05: In September 2026, how much more did we keep per order in store than on a DoorDash delivery order?

WITH september AS (
  SELECT o.channel, o.fulfillment_type, o.gross_sales_cents,
         o.gross_sales_cents - o.discount_cents AS after_discount,
         coalesce(p.processing_fee_cents, 0) AS fee
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.id AND p.status = 'completed'
  WHERE o.state = 'completed'
    AND date_trunc('month', o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago') = '2026-09-01'
)
SELECT round(
    avg(after_discount - fee) FILTER (WHERE channel = 'in_store')
  - avg(after_discount - gross_sales_cents * 0.25) FILTER (WHERE channel = 'doordash' AND fulfillment_type = 'delivery')
)
FROM september

I didn't file this dispute, because the window has closed. Order 195145 was a completed DoorDash order placed on 2026-09-29. It had three items and a gross of $42.37. DoorDash allows 7 days from the order date, and that ran out about 18 days ago. Today is 2026-10-24, which is 25 days after the order. A dispute filed after the window is rejected automatically [Marketplace Terms §3, Missing or Incorrect Items].

The order has no identified customer, so the repeat-dispute rule for flagged customers can't apply [Marketplace Terms §7, Repeat Disputes]. The chargeback would normally stand. The order was over $40, so it should have a packing photo. That photo can't save a dispute filed this late.

If you'd like, I can propose a notice to you about this order so the chargeback can be logged.

case.question: Text everyone who gave us a phone number: 10% off pho this weekend.
case.note: There are 29,762 customers with phone numbers, but only 563 with verified consent. The action checker must use 563 for the audience. That exceeds the 500-customer limit, so the proposal requires the owner's approval and remains pending.

trace.question: Text everyone who gave us a phone number: 10% off pho this weekend.
trace.answer:
I've drafted the text campaign, but nothing has been sent. It's waiting for your approval.

I limited it to 563 customers, not everyone who gave us a phone number. Of the 29,762 customers with a phone number, 563 have verified SMS consent and haven't unsubscribed. The policy allows marketing texts only to customers with verified consent. The 17,626 who only gave us their number when ordering don't qualify, and neither do the 848 who unsubscribed [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts].

The draft reads: "Mekong Noodle House: enjoy 10% off any pho this weekend, through Sunday Oct 25, 2026. One per customer. Reply STOP to opt out"

The checks passed on these points:
- **Discount size:** 10% is under the 15% cap [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].
- **Offer wording:** the message has an expiry date and says "one per customer" [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].
- **Required wording:** it names the restaurant and ends with the opt-out line [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording].
- **Audience:** 563 customers, all with a phone, verified consent and no unsubscribe.

Because 563 is over the 500-person cap, you have to approve it yourself.

Each customer can get at most four marketing texts in a calendar month [Customer Messaging Policy §4, Frequency]. I haven't checked how many texts these customers have already had this month.

case.question: Text our regulars 25% off Seasonal Specials this week.
case.note: Ridgeline's messaging policy caps discounts at 20% without approval and prohibits discounting Seasonal Specials in messages. The requested campaign should not reach human review as an allowed proposal.

trace.question: Text our regulars 25% off Seasonal Specials this week.
trace.answer:
I can't set up this text. Seasonal Specials may never be discounted in a message, and 25% is also over the 20% limit that applies without your approval [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages]. The ban on discounting Seasonal Specials holds even with your approval, so I haven't proposed the campaign.

Here are two options that would be allowed:
- **Different item:** a text for regulars with an offer of 20% or less on something other than Seasonal Specials. It would have to expire within 7 days and apply once per customer.
- **No offer:** a text that mentions the Seasonal Specials but includes no discount.

Regulars are customers with four or more completed orders in a month [Definitions §2, Regulars]. For marketing texts, they would also need to have ordered in the last 90 days and have a phone number on file. Otherwise they need verified SMS consent [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Texts]. Each text must name Ridgeline Coffee and end with "Text STOP to stop" [Customer Messaging Policy §6, Required Wording].

If you want either option, tell me which and I'll count the audience and draft the message.

case.question: Comp the $60 ticket for table 12, the pho was cold.
case.note: A manager's comp limit is $25, so a $60 comp requires the owner's approval. The data also has no table-number field, so the agent cannot identify the order from 'table 12' alone.

trace.question: Comp the $60 ticket for table 12, the pho was cold.
trace.answer:
I haven't comped anything. I proposed a request to notify the owner, and it's pending approval.

A $60 comp is over the $25 a manager can comp on one ticket. Anything above that needs the owner, Linh, who can be reached by text during service [House Policy §2, Comps]. A cold dish is a valid reason for a comp under that section. A comp of $25 or less could be handled by the manager on duty.

I also couldn't match table 12 to a specific order. The data has no table numbers, and several in-store orders in the $50–$70 range came in around the same time. The proposal therefore has no order attached. Someone will need to tell Linh which ticket it is, or link the order when she approves.
